Astrondeu can spend **10 Mind Points** to apply any of the symbols below to a creature he can see. The PCs can spend **1 Fabula Point** to avoid this effect. 
- **Symbol of Despair**: When the creature bearing this symbol recovers *Hit Points* and/or *Mind Points* during conflicts, instead they only recover **half** the normal amount of *Hit Points* and/or *Mind Points*, respectively.
- **Symbol of Forbiddance**: When you create this symbol, choose an action type: **Attack**, **Guard**, **Objective**, **Spell**, or **Skill**. When the creature bearing this symbol performs the chosen action, they lose **5 Hit Points** and **5 Mind Points** (before performing that action). Both amounts increse to **10** if you are **level 20 or higher**, or to **20** if you are **level 40 or higher**.
- **Symbol of Weakness**: When you create this symbol, choose a damage type: **air**, **bolt**, **dark**, **earth**, **fire**, **ice**, **light**, or **poison**. The creature bearing this symbol suffers **5 extra damage** from sources dealing damage of the chosen type.
- **Symbol of Fragility**: When you create this symbol, choose a damage type: **air**, **bolt**, **dark**, **earth**, **fire**, **ice**, **light**, or **poison**. The creature bearing this symbol gain **vulnerability** of the chosen type.

Additionally, he can charge against a creature by spending **1 Ultima Poin**t, stripping it of any assistance it is receiving. This includes spells, magitechs, magiseeds, dances, verses, invocations, symbols, clearing the brainwave clock, and even forcing the dismissal of arcanums. In other words, any positive effect gained through **Skills**. Astrondeu can use this ability only once per round.
The PCs can spend **1 Fabula Point** to completely negate this effect.

r3tpzfDN4fuyXPRz20bf.description: The embodiment of greed. Meticulous and cunning, he ensnares all who catch his interest. notes.name: Final considerations.
notes.effect:
Astrondeu is a cunning villain, and his strategies depend on which Summoned Servants you bring into battle. Using unique creatures with distinct traits is a good approach.

He also utilizes Symbolist mechanics, so if no PC is using symbols, consider not including Astrondeu.

Additionally, Astrondeu is an unbalanced and punishing villain, designed specifically to discourage players from facing him and to lower the party’s morale. Overcoming his immunity to all damage is meant to be a campaign objective.

Finally, Astrondeu has absolute confidence in his own immortality, so he has no mechanics related to entering crisis. However, if you want to strengthen him even further, consider making him vulnerable to all damage by default—his special rule compensates for this, and the extra skill points can add variety. But if you want to make the fight even more intense, consider giving him resistance to all damage after losing his immortality.

special.effect:
Astrondeu has a vast collection of specimens and never appears alone in battle. He is always accompanied by a number of **rank soldier** creatures equal to the number of players **minus one**.
And every time a creature reaches 0 HP, another identical one appears in its place in the end of this creature next turn.

**Ninjas**--the fastest and most dextrous of the Nobodies--are comparatively rare. Or, they may just be so quick and stealthy that their targets either never see them or never live to tell the tale.

As the deadly shock troopers of the Nobody ranks, **Ninjas** rarely work alongside other types of Nobodies. Instead, they operate in small squads with other **Ninjas**, often deep in enemy territory.
